free_tier.stated: free disposable inbox with a keyless REST API; no signup and no stated byte quota; unlimited inbox count
free_tier.notes: The FAQ states 100% free with no limits and unlimited inboxes. No per-inbox byte quota is stated on the first-party pages reviewed.

per_object_cap.stated: no message or object byte cap is stated on the first-party API docs, FAQ, home page or official SDK pages
per_object_cap.notes: unverified: no per-message size number appears on any first-party NenzMail page reviewed

retention.stated: Inboxes auto-delete after 1 hour (3600 seconds); on expiry or manual delete all emails are permanently removed and cannot be recovered
retention.notes: Retention is one hour, below a day. days is null because no day count is stated.

egress.terms: inbound messages are received at no charge; free outbound send through POST /api/send, rate limited to 20 emails per inbox per hour; no egress metering or traffic price is stated

interface_detail: Keyless REST API on api.nenzmail.com: POST /api/inbox/create, GET /api/inbox/:address/emails, GET /api/email/:id, POST /api/send, DELETE /api/inbox/:address; all responses JSON, CORS enabled.
tooling: curl or any HTTP client; official SDK packages nenzmail on PyPI (Python) and nenzmail on npm (Node.js)
chaining: Create a disposable inbox with a keyless POST, let a service deliver a verification email over SMTP, poll GET /api/inbox/:address/emails, read the full message through GET /api/email/:id, then delete the inbox. The 1-hour auto-delete clamps the whole chain, and outbound send is capped at 20 emails per inbox per hour.

limits.value: Inboxes auto-delete after 1 hour (3600 seconds); emails are permanently removed on expiry
outbound send rate limited to 20 emails per inbox per hour
Rate limits may apply for abuse prevention; no numeric request cap is published on the API docs

binding_note: the 1-hour auto-delete removes an unread message before any request-rate or send cap is reached, so the retention window decides what a chain can do

identity_cost.detail: No signup, no phone number, no personal information required; the API needs no key, token or account: 'No API key, no token, no signup.'

reliability_note: The live host nenzmail.com returned HTTP 502 at review; the pages used here are Wayback snapshots dated 2026-10-28. A deleted or expired inbox cannot be recovered. No numeric message-size cap was stated on the first-party pages reviewed.
confidence_note: values from first-party API docs, FAQ, home page and official SDK pages; the vendor site was read from archive after the live host returned 502; no probe was run, so the rung is documented and not measured

evidence.quote: NenzMail is free and open. No API key, no token, no signup. Just use your inbox address to read and send emails. Inboxes auto-delete after 1 hour.
evidence.proved: inbox creation and API access are anonymous and keyless, and retention is one hour
the retention clamp is one hour, expressed in seconds

evidence.quote: Rate limits may apply for abuse prevention
evidence.proved: the API docs warn of rate limiting without publishing a numeric request cap

evidence.quote: Yes, 100% free with no limits. Create as many temporary inboxes as you need.
evidence.proved: the free tier has no stated byte quota and the inbox count is unlimited

evidence.quote: NenzMail provides a free REST API for creating inboxes, listing emails, and reading email content.
evidence.proved: a free REST API covers inbox creation, listing and reading

evidence.quote: No signup, no phone number, no personal information required.
evidence.proved: registration needs no email, phone, card or identity document
the official SDK exposes three selectable inbox domains

evidence.quote: Send an email from your inbox to any address. Rate limited: 20/hr per inbox.
evidence.proved: outbound send is capped at 20 emails per inbox per hour

notes: Domain count and domain names come from the official SDK pages; the web and API pages use nenzmail.com while the SDK defaults to nenzmail.xyz. Per-inbox byte size and per-message byte cap are unverified: no first-party page states a number.
